title: Stripe API degradation causing silent cross-signal latency cascade
root_cause: Stripe API began returning intermittent 503s and 429s during a traffic spike. The checkout service retried silently up to 3 times before returning HTTP 200. Each retry added 1-2 seconds. No single signal crossed a threshold — p99 latency crept up gradually, error rate hovered at 1.8%, throughput dropped 42% as users abandoned. The combination of all three signals told the story.
business_impact: 312 customers double-charged due to non-idempotent retries. Throughput dropped 42% over 55 minutes. $89,000 revenue impact.
resolution: Added idempotency keys to all Stripe API calls. Implemented circuit breaker on payment-gateway. Added cross-signal alert: if p99 > 2x baseline AND error_rate > 1% AND throughput_drop > 20% simultaneously, page immediately.
runbook: 1. Check Stripe status: https://status.stripe.com. 2. Check idempotency key collisions in logs: grep 'idempotency key collision'. 3. Identify duplicate charges: query orders WHERE created_at BETWEEN incident_start AND incident_end GROUP BY user_id HAVING count > 1. 4. Issue refunds for duplicates. 5. Enable circuit breaker: CIRCUIT_BREAKER_ENABLED=true.

signal_correlation.metrics: p99 latency rose from 210ms to 4300ms over 45 minutes
signal_correlation.traces: payment-gateway span consuming 94% of total trace duration
signal_correlation.logs: repeated retry warnings followed by idempotency collision errors

title: Metric shows healthy, logs show silent failures — ML model serving divergence
root_cause: The recommendations API reported HTTP 200 and normal latency metrics. However, logs showed the ML model was returning empty arrays for 34% of requests. The metrics dashboard showed green — response time was fine, error rate was 0%. Only log analysis revealed that 'success' responses contained no actual recommendations.
business_impact: 34% of users received empty recommendations for 6 hours. Estimated 18% drop in cross-sell revenue. Metrics-only monitoring gave zero indication of the problem.
resolution: Added payload validation metric: track response_body_size_bytes as a separate metric. Alert when p50 of response_body_size drops below 100 bytes for endpoints expected to return data. Added log-metric correlation check.
runbook: 1. Check response body size metrics: if avg(response_body_size) < 100 bytes on /api/recommendations, escalate. 2. Verify ML model health: curl /api/recommendations/health. 3. Check model serving logs for empty array responses. 4. Enable fallback: RECOMMENDATION_FALLBACK=true.

signal_correlation.metrics: HTTP 200, normal latency, 0% error rate - all green
signal_correlation.logs: 34% of responses contain empty recommendations array

title: 42% throughput drop with no error rate increase — users abandoning silently
root_cause: Checkout throughput dropped from 142 RPS to 82 RPS over 50 minutes. No error rate increase — HTTP 200 throughout. No latency spike on successful completions. The drop was caused by users abandoning the checkout flow mid-way due to slow payment processing, never reaching the error state. The system looked healthy. Users were leaving.
business_impact: 42% of checkout attempts abandoned. Revenue impact proportional to abandonment increase. Invisible to all standard monitors.
resolution: Added abandonment rate tracking: measure checkout_started vs checkout_completed ratio. Alert when completion rate drops below 80%. Correlate with session drop-off metrics.
runbook: 1. Check checkout completion rate: checkout_completed / checkout_started for the window. 2. If completion rate < 80%, check payment gateway latency. 3. Check user session traces for abandoned checkout flows. 4. Correlate throughput drop with any recent deployment or dependency degradation.

signal_correlation.metrics: throughput dropped 42%, error rate 0%, latency normal for completions
signal_correlation.traces: no failed traces - abandoned sessions simply stop
signal_correlation.logs: no errors - abandonment leaves no log trace

title: Single dependency span consuming 94% of trace duration — silent bottleneck
root_cause: Distributed traces showed checkout completing successfully at HTTP 200. However, trace analysis revealed the payment-gateway span was consuming 3,980ms out of a 4,250ms total trace — 94% of total duration. All other spans (inventory, notification) were healthy at under 50ms. The bottleneck was invisible in aggregate metrics because the overall success rate was maintained through retries.
business_impact: Users experienced 4+ second checkout times. 31% abandonment rate increase. Trace analysis identified the bottleneck 30 minutes faster than metrics-only monitoring.
resolution: Added span-level SLA alerts: if any single span consumes more than 80% of parent trace duration AND parent duration > 2x baseline, alert immediately. Added payment-gateway specific latency SLO: p99 < 500ms.
runbook: 1. Query traces: filter spans WHERE duration_ms > parent_duration * 0.8. 2. Identify the bottleneck service. 3. Check that service's own metrics and logs. 4. For payment-gateway: check Stripe dashboard for API degradation. 5. Implement circuit breaker if bottleneck persists > 10 minutes.

signal_correlation.metrics: aggregate p99 rising but not obviously alarming
signal_correlation.traces: payment-gateway span = 94% of total trace duration
signal_correlation.logs: retry warnings in checkout-api correlate with slow payment-gateway spans
